newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco talks on lawsuits to resume Monday.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco talks on lawsuits to resume Monday.

text.p: Cigarette makers and state attorneys general are scheduled to resume negotiations Monday aimed at resolving how to handle mounting litigation against the tobacco industry and other issues.
The talks are to be held in Dallas with key negotiator Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore expected to arrive here later Sunday night.

The attorneys general, who have sued the industry to recoup Medicaid costs of smokers, are united in the stance that any settlement would exclude total immunity from all lawsuits. The parties are attempting to find other ways to reach a settlement and among the proposals is one that would allow individual suits but would place a ceiling on maximum liability.

The negotiations will resume at the same time as a Jacksonville, Fla. jury begins its first full day of deliberations in a lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings, brought by the family of a smoker who died of lung cancer. The case went to the jury Friday evening.

The case is widely-watched as the plaintiff's lawyer, Norwood Wilner won a verdict against Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp., a unit of B.A.T Industries P.L.C., last year. The verdict caused tobacco stocks to drop sharply. It was only the second time a jury had awarded damages against the industry.
